families.name: Policy Gradient GANs
families.definition: Methods that use reinforcement learning to propagate gradients from the discriminator to the generator for discrete text generation.

properties.text: These methods address the non-differentiability of discrete text outputs by treating generation as a sequential decision process.
The discriminator provides a scalar reward signal that guides the generator's policy updates.
SeqGAN is a foundational approach in this family that uses policy gradient to train sequence generative adversarial nets.
ReGAN extends this by using RE[LAX|BAR|INFORCE] estimators for sequence generation.
Boundary-Seeking GANs use the discriminator's difference measure to compute importance weights for policy gradients.
Long Text Generation via Adversarial Training with Leaked Information uses intermediate information to guide the generative process beyond just the final scalar reward.

limitations.text: These methods suffer from high variance in gradient estimates.
The scalar guiding signal is only available after the entire text is generated, lacking intermediate structural information.
Training can be inefficient compared to direct backpropagation methods.
They often face issues of reward sparsity and mode collapse.

families.name: Continuous Approximation GANs
families.definition: Methods that use continuous relaxations of discrete distributions, such as Gumbel-Softmax, to enable gradient flow in text GANs.

properties.text: Gumbel-Softmax provides a differentiable sample from a categorical distribution that can be smoothly annealed.
These methods allow standard backpropagation through the generator by approximating discrete choices with continuous variables.
GANS for Sequences of Discrete Elements with the Gumbel-softmax Distribution evaluates RNNs with Gumbel-Softmax output distributions.
Categorical Reparameterization with Gumbel-Softmax presents an efficient gradient estimator for stochastic neural networks with categorical latent variables.

limitations.text: The continuous approximation may not perfectly capture the discrete nature of text during training.
Performance depends on the annealing schedule to transition from continuous to discrete distributions.

families.name: Latent Space and Feature Matching GANs
families.definition: Methods that operate on continuous latent representations or match feature distributions to avoid direct discrete gradient issues.

properties.text: Adversarial Text Generation Without Reinforcement Learning uses an autoencoder to learn a low-dimensional continuous representation of sentences.
Latent Code and Text-based Generative Adversarial Networks for Soft-text Generation use autoencoders to provide continuous 'soft-text' representations for discrimination.
Adversarial Feature Matching for Text Generation matches high-dimensional latent feature distributions of real and synthetic sentences using a kernelized discrepancy metric.
Adversarial Text Generation via Feature-Mover's Distance uses a metric inspired by optimal transport to match latent feature distributions.
Generating Text through Adversarial Training Using Skip-Thought Vectors uses sentence embeddings to model writing style.
Text Generation Based on Generative Adversarial Nets with Latent Variable combines VAEs with GANs to use high-level latent random variables for learning data distribution.

limitations.text: Reliance on the quality of the learned latent representation or autoencoder.
May struggle to capture fine-grained discrete details if the latent space is too compressed.

families.name: Enhanced Discriminator and Reward GANs
families.definition: Methods that modify the discriminator architecture or reward function to provide richer guidance and improve training stability.

properties.text: TextGAIL uses large pre-trained language models to provide more reliable reward guidance for the discriminator.
Self-Adversarial Learning with Comparative Discrimination for Text Generation employs a pairwise classifier to compare text quality between samples.
Adversarial Ranking for Language Generation (RankGAN) trains the discriminator to rank a collection of samples rather than assigning binary predicates.
Diversity-Promoting GAN (DP-GAN) uses a language-model based discriminator to distinguish novel text from repeated text.
FGGAN: Feature-Guiding Generative Adversarial Networks for Text Generation uses feature-guiding to solve the problem of weak scalar reward signals.
Improved Training of Wasserstein GANs proposes penalizing the norm of the gradient of the critic to enforce Lipschitz constraints instead of weight clipping.
Maximum-Likelihood Augmented Discrete Generative Adversarial Networks derive a low-variance objective using the discriminator's output to augment maximum likelihood.

limitations.text: Complexity in designing effective ranking or comparative discriminators.
May require additional pre-trained models or complex loss functions.

families.name: Conditional and Constrained GANs
families.definition: Methods that incorporate specific conditions, constraints, or multi-modal information to control text generation.

properties.text: Customizable text generation via conditional text generative adversarial network allows for generating text with specific attributes.
BFGAN: Backward and Forward Generative Adversarial Networks for Lexically Constrained Sentence Generation uses backward and forward generators to incorporate lexical constraints.
A Generative Model for category text generation (CS-GAN) combines RL, GANs, and RNNs to generate category-specific sentences.
Automatic generation of sentimental texts via mixture adversarial networks (SentiGAN) uses multiple generators and a multi-class discriminator for sentiment-labeled text.
Emotional Text Generation Based on Cross-Domain Sentiment Transfer uses GANs for cross-domain sentiment transfer to generate emotional text.
QuGAN: Quasi Generative Adversarial Network for Tibetan Question Answering Corpus Generation is designed for low-resource language QA corpus generation.

limitations.text: Requires specific conditional inputs or labels which may not always be available.
May struggle with the quality-diversity trade-off in constrained settings.

families.name: Hybrid and Alternative Training Paradigms
families.definition: Methods that combine GANs with other learning frameworks like imitation learning, inverse reinforcement learning, or curriculum learning.

properties.text: TextGAIL proposes a generative adversarial imitation learning framework for text generation.
Toward Diverse Text Generation with Inverse Reinforcement Learning employs IRL to learn a reward function and optimal policy.
Language Generation with Recurrent Generative Adversarial Networks without Pre-training uses curriculum learning to train RNNs from scratch.
Objective-Reinforced Generative Adversarial Networks (ORGAN) combines GANs and RL to bias generation towards desirable metrics.
Meta-CoTGAN: A Meta Cooperative Training Paradigm for Improving Adversarial Text Generation uses meta cooperative training to address mode collapse.
DGSAN: Discrete Generative Self-Adversarial Network proposes a self-adversarial network for discrete data generation.

limitations.text: Increased computational complexity due to multiple training phases or objectives.
Sensitivity to hyperparameters in hybrid frameworks.
GANs for text generation often perform worse than their Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) counterparts.
There is a lack of a reliable guiding signal in discriminators for text GANs.
Adversarial training suffers from a quality-diversity trade-off due to mode collapse.
The discrete nature of text hinders the direct application of standard GAN objectives due to non-differentiability.
Training instability and convergence issues remain significant challenges in text GANs.
Existing methods struggle to generate text that rivals the quality and diversity of human-generated text.
Most machines output fixed-length text or generate text that is too similar to the input training text.
There is an imbalance between generator and discriminator causing overfitting in sequence-based text adversarial networks.
Reward sparsity affects the quality and diversity of generated samples in conventional GANs.
It remains difficult to fully discover local and global feature information between layers in deep CNNs for character recognition.
